currentContext.expansion: The Company's expansion programme sits under its Vision-2030 roadmap and is stated to be under way as planned. During FY26 it completed the expansion of Pentaerythritol and Phenolic Resin capacities; having recently commissioned the extra Phenolic Resin capacity it is further adding to that capacity, which is under construction. Two new product platforms are being built: a new Triacetin plant and a Multi-Purpose Plant for the manufacture of Pentaerythritol derivatives and specialty chemicals, both described as in advanced stages of construction / implementation and expected to commence commercial operations 'shortly' - no dated commissioning is given. Manufacturing remains at the three integrated chemical sites at Ankleshwar (Gujarat), Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and Naidupeta (Andhra Pradesh). The R&D team and infrastructure have been significantly augmented. At the wholly owned Ethiopian denim subsidiary Kanoria Africa Textiles Plc, capacity utilisation improved to 66% from 56% and the Board is evaluating an addition of weaving capacity in the near term, for which incremental capital expenditure is expected to be moderate/modest because surplus capacity already exists in the other departments. Funding: the Company changed its Authorized Capital to Rs 100 crore at an EGM on 1 April 2026 and, to meet capital expenditure, working capital and general corporate purposes, issued 4,95,000 redeemable 7% Preference Shares of Rs 1,000 each at par to M/s. R. V. Investment and Dealers Limited on 18 April 2026, aggregating Rs 49,50,00,000 (stated as Rs Forty-Nine Crores and Fifty Lakhs). No installed-capacity table (tonnage or similar) was disclosed in the routed text.

risks.risk: Raw material, energy and foreign-exchange price volatility
risks.note: Listed by management as a main business risk: 'Volatility in raw material, energy, and foreign exchange markets, which may impact operating costs and profitability.' The Company also flags that inordinate fluctuations in Methanol and Phenol prices, driven by crude oil volatility and rupee depreciation against the US Dollar, may raise operating costs and cause FX losses. Raw material prices were described as wildly volatile during the year, with availability itself at times uncertain.

risks.risk: Low-cost import competition in key products
risks.note: Management flags increasing competition from low-cost imports, particularly in Sodium Formate and Hexamine, which may pressure domestic pricing and market share. The Directors' Report adds that some products faced stiff price competition from overseas competitors dumping into India because other markets were unavailable to them on account of sanctions. Continued influx of low-priced imports is cited as one reason overall financial performance remains under pressure.

Cited as a main business risk: geopolitical uncertainties and competition from low-cost imports may adversely impact business performance. Ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, changes in global trade dynamics and disruptions in international supply chains may adversely impact raw material availability, logistics, energy costs and overall operations. The Russia-Ukraine conflict and Middle East disturbances are named as having created challenges through the year, including uncertain raw material availability and adversely affected demand.

risks.risk: Export-market and tariff exposure in Hexamine
risks.note: Structural concentration risk: Hexamine exports to Europe and the USA together account for a significant percentage of the Company's Hexamine production, and during the year suffered from lack of demand (Europe) and high tariffs (USA).
Listed by management as a main business risk: 'Changes in government regulations, environmental compliance requirements, and trade policies affecting the chemical industry.'

risks.risk: Ethiopia country risk at the wholly owned denim subsidiary (KAT)
risks.note: KAT remains exposed to macroeconomic risks including currency volatility, inflation and changes in government policy in Ethiopia; increased domestic competition and shortage of foreign currency may impact margins. Mitigation stated: close monitoring plus cost optimization and customer diversification.

risks.risk: Process safety and EHS risk inherent to chemical manufacturing
risks.note: Managed through the Environment, Health, Safety and Sustainability (EHSS) framework, proactive risk assessment, process safety management, safety training and a dedicated HAZOP team that identifies and mitigates process safety risks across manufacturing operations. The Company reported zero reportable accidents and zero lost time injuries across all manufacturing units during the year.

risks.risk: Cyclicality and demand volatility in the chemicals cycle
risks.note: Management states demand was adversely affected 'as is usually the case in times of unusual volatility and uncertainty', and that the Alco Chemicals Division's financial performance remains under pressure from intense market competition. The Board states it does not foresee any risk which may threaten the existence of the Company; the Risk Management Committee (R.V. Kanoria as Chairman, S.V. Kanoria, S.K. Birla and Group CFO N.K. Nolkha) met twice during FY26.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Kanoria Chemicals & Industries Limited (KCIL) is a Kolkata-headquartered alco-chemicals and specialty chemicals manufacturer operating three integrated Indian plants, which also runs integrated denim manufacturing in Ethiopia through its wholly owned subsidiary Kanoria Africa Textiles Plc.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company's Alco Chemicals Division manufactures Formaldehyde, Pentaerythritol, Hexamine, Sodium Formate, Phenolic Resins, Acetaldehyde and other value-added chemical products at integrated facilities at Ankleshwar (Gujarat), Vizag/Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and Naidupeta (Andhra Pradesh), selling into construction, infrastructure, laminates, plywood, paints, pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and specialty chemicals end-users. It exports Hexamine to Europe and the USA, which together account for a significant percentage of its Hexamine production. Its second business is integrated denim manufacturing in Ethiopia, carried out through wholly owned subsidiary Kanoria Africa Textiles PLC ('KAT'); the Company states there has been no change in the nature of its business during the year.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Outlook for the Chemicals business is stated as positive, supported by India's strong economic fundamentals, increasing industrial activity and growing demand from key end-user industries
- Continued focus on capacity expansion, product diversification, operational excellence and value-added specialty chemicals is expected to strengthen market position and support sustainable long-term growth
- Upon commercialization, the Triacetin and Penta Derivatives platforms are expected to diversify the product portfolio, strengthen the position in value-added specialty chemicals and create new avenues for growth
- Alco Chemicals financial performance is said to remain under pressure from intense market competition, volatility in key raw material prices and continued influx of low-priced imports in certain product categories
- Business remains exposed to geopolitical developments, volatility in raw material and energy prices, FX fluctuations and increasing low-cost import competition
- In Ethiopia, the Government's currency devaluation and economic liberalization measures boosted demand for locally manufactured products, marking a sharp recovery for KAT; capacity utilisation improved to 66% from 56%
- Demand for denim fabric remained robust despite intensifying competition in the local Ethiopian market; sales growth momentum is expected to sustain and the encouraging trend has continued into the current year
- KAT remains exposed to Ethiopian currency volatility, inflation, government policy change, domestic competition and shortage of foreign currency, which may impact margins
- Chairman's statement on the Ethiopian denim business: 'Based on the orders presently on hand, we expect this momentum to continue.' - no order-book quantum is disclosed.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Pursue the long-term strategic roadmap 'Vision 2030' for sustainable growth in domestic and international markets and enhanced profitability; future expansion plans towards this roadmap are stated to be under way as planned
- Expand existing manufacturing capacities - completed expansion of Pentaerythritol and Resin capacities during the year, with further Phenolic Resin capacity under construction
- Move up the value chain into value-added specialty chemicals by developing two new product platforms, Triacetin and Penta Derivatives, both in advanced stages of implementation
- Drive innovation through a dedicated New Product Development (NPD) Cell across the Chemicals and Resin businesses (new products, process improvements, application-specific solutions)
- Significantly augment the R&D team and infrastructure, targeting product innovation, materials for new applications, and waste elimination / waste-to-wealth generation
- Focus on cost optimization, process and product innovation through R&D, and strengthening of the supply chain - the three levers management credits for FY26's improved chemicals performance
- Focus on innovation, cost competitiveness, supply chain resilience and prudent risk management to address geopolitical, raw-material, energy, FX and import-competition pressures
- At the Ethiopian denim subsidiary (KAT), capitalise on recovering demand by evaluating an addition of weaving capacity, while mitigating country risk through cost optimization and customer diversification
- Maintain the Responsible Care affiliation and sustainable-manufacturing practices (renewable energy adoption, waste minimization, water conservation, waste heat recovery, resource recycling)
- Strengthen existing businesses and pursue new opportunities only 'where they make economic sense', with a prudent, long-term capital-allocation posture (Chairman's statement)
- Stated philosophy (Note 43, Capital Management): being in a capital intensive industry, the objective is to maintain a strong credit rating and healthy capital ratios and to establish a capital structure that maximises return to stakeholders through an optimum mix of debt and equity. The Company says it regularly considers financing and refinancing opportunities to diversify its debt profile, reduce interest cost and lengthen the maturity of its debt portfolio, and closely monitors judicious allocation of capital amongst competing capital expansion projects and strategic acquisitions to capture market opportunities at minimum risk. Its capital requirement is mainly to fund capacity expansion, repayment of principal and interest on borrowings and strategic acquisitions; the principal source of funding has been and is expected to remain cash generated from operations, supplemented by bank borrowings and the capital markets. It is not subject to any externally imposed capital requirements and monitors capital using the gearing ratio (net debt to total equity). On distributions, the Board did not recommend any dividend for FY2025-26 and no amount was transferred to Reserves; a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy is published on the Company's website. Care Ratings reaffirmed the long-term bank facility rating at CARE BB+ Stable and short-term at CARE A4+. Fresh capital for capex/working capital was raised post year-end via a Rs 49.50 crore issue of 7% redeemable preference shares to a related party (R. V. Investment and Dealers Limited) after raising Authorized Capital to Rs 100 crore. Governance around related-party dealings: all FY26 RPTs were stated to be in the ordinary course of business and at arm's length, approved by the Audit Committee and Board with shareholder approval by postal ballot; no material RPTs above the materiality threshold were entered, so AOC-2 was not applicable.
- Maintains affiliation with the Responsible Care Logo ('RC Logo') initiative and holds Responsible Care certification for the Ankleshwar and Vizag plant locations for the period May 2024 to April 2027
- All three manufacturing units (Ankleshwar, Vishakhapatnam, Naidupeta) maintained ISO 14001 environmental management and ISO 45001 occupational health and safety certification (alongside ISO 9001) throughout the year
- Zero Accident culture: zero reportable accidents and zero lost time injuries across all manufacturing units during the year
- Environmental and resource conservation initiatives implemented: renewable energy adoption, waste minimization, water conservation, waste heat recovery and resource recycling
- R&D focus explicitly includes waste elimination and waste-to-wealth generation alongside product innovation
- EHSS framework strengthened through continuous improvement, proactive risk assessment, process safety management and regular safety awareness/training, supported by a dedicated HAZOP team
- CSR Policy in place with stated focus areas: environmental sustainability and ecological balance; promoting education and employment-enhancing vocational skills; gender equality and women's empowerment (including homes/hostels for women and orphans, old age homes, day care centres for senior citizens); rural development; and socio-economic development and welfare of SC/ST/OBC, minorities and women. The Directors' Report states there is no unspent amount towards CSR expenses
- Governance-side ESG: Whistle Blower Policy / vigil mechanism for Directors, employees and other stakeholders covering unethical behaviour, fraud, legal violations and leak of unpublished price sensitive information, with access to the Audit Committee Chairman; no employee was denied access to the Audit Committee during the year
- No quantified ESG targets (emissions, energy, water intensity or similar) were disclosed in the routed text - a BRSR section was not included in this bundle

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's expansion programme sits under its Vision-2030 roadmap and is stated to be under way as planned. During FY26 it completed the expansion of Pentaerythritol and Phenolic Resin capacities; having recently commissioned the extra Phenolic Resin capacity it is further adding to that capacity, which is under construction. Two new product platforms are being built: a new Triacetin plant and a Multi-Purpose Plant for the manufacture of Pentaerythritol derivatives and specialty chemicals, both described as in advanced stages of construction / implementation and expected to commence commercial operations 'shortly' - no dated commissioning is given. Manufacturing remains at the three integrated chemical sites at Ankleshwar (Gujarat), Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and Naidupeta (Andhra Pradesh). The R&D team and infrastructure have been significantly augmented. At the wholly owned Ethiopian denim subsidiary Kanoria Africa Textiles Plc, capacity utilisation improved to 66% from 56% and the Board is evaluating an addition of weaving capacity in the near term, for which incremental capital expenditure is expected to be moderate/modest because surplus capacity already exists in the other departments. Funding: the Company changed its Authorized Capital to Rs 100 crore at an EGM on 1 April 2026 and, to meet capital expenditure, working capital and general corporate purposes, issued 4,95,000 redeemable 7% Preference Shares of Rs 1,000 each at par to M/s. R. V. Investment and Dealers Limited on 18 April 2026, aggregating Rs 49,50,00,000 (stated as Rs Forty-Nine Crores and Fifty Lakhs). No installed-capacity table (tonnage or similar) was disclosed in the routed text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- States it continues to hold a leading position in most of its key product segments, supported by a diversified product portfolio, strong customer relationships, advanced manufacturing capabilities and a focus on operational excellence
- Manufacturing technologies for Pentaerythritol, Hexamine, Phenolic Resins, Triacetin and Penta Derivatives have been developed and continuously enhanced in-house
- Formaldehyde plants based on advanced process technologies giving high operational efficiency, consistent product quality and optimized energy utilization
- Integrated manufacturing footprint across three Indian sites (Ankleshwar, Vizag, Naidupeta) serving a diverse range of end-user industries
- Dedicated New Product Development (NPD) Cell driving innovation across the Chemicals and Resin businesses; R&D team and infrastructure significantly augmented during the year
- ISO 9001/14001/45001 certified units plus Responsible Care certification, positioning it among chemical enterprises recognised for safety and environmental standards
- Excellent safety record maintained during the year with zero reportable accidents and zero lost time injuries across all manufacturing units

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw material, energy and foreign-exchange price volatility — Listed by management as a main business risk: 'Volatility in raw material, energy, and foreign exchange markets, which may impact operating costs and profitability.' The Company also flags that inordinate fluctuations in Methanol and Phenol prices, driven by crude oil volatility and rupee depreciation against the US Dollar, may raise operating costs and cause FX losses. Raw material prices were described as wildly volatile during the year, with availability itself at times uncertain.
- Low-cost import competition in key products — Management flags increasing competition from low-cost imports, particularly in Sodium Formate and Hexamine, which may pressure domestic pricing and market share. The Directors' Report adds that some products faced stiff price competition from overseas competitors dumping into India because other markets were unavailable to them on account of sanctions. Continued influx of low-priced imports is cited as one reason overall financial performance remains under pressure.
- Geopolitical uncertainty and supply-chain disruption — Cited as a main business risk: geopolitical uncertainties and competition from low-cost imports may adversely impact business performance. Ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, changes in global trade dynamics and disruptions in international supply chains may adversely impact raw material availability, logistics, energy costs and overall operations. The Russia-Ukraine conflict and Middle East disturbances are named as having created challenges through the year, including uncertain raw material availability and adversely affected demand.
- Export-market and tariff exposure in Hexamine — Structural concentration risk: Hexamine exports to Europe and the USA together account for a significant percentage of the Company's Hexamine production, and during the year suffered from lack of demand (Europe) and high tariffs (USA).
- Regulatory, environmental-compliance and trade-policy change — Listed by management as a main business risk: 'Changes in government regulations, environmental compliance requirements, and trade policies affecting the chemical industry.'
- Ethiopia country risk at the wholly owned denim subsidiary (KAT) — KAT remains exposed to macroeconomic risks including currency volatility, inflation and changes in government policy in Ethiopia; increased domestic competition and shortage of foreign currency may impact margins. Mitigation stated: close monitoring plus cost optimization and customer diversification.
- Process safety and EHS risk inherent to chemical manufacturing — Managed through the Environment, Health, Safety and Sustainability (EHSS) framework, proactive risk assessment, process safety management, safety training and a dedicated HAZOP team that identifies and mitigates process safety risks across manufacturing operations. The Company reported zero reportable accidents and zero lost time injuries across all manufacturing units during the year.
- Cyclicality and demand volatility in the chemicals cycle — Management states demand was adversely affected 'as is usually the case in times of unusual volatility and uncertainty', and that the Alco Chemicals Division's financial performance remains under pressure from intense market competition. The Board states it does not foresee any risk which may threaten the existence of the Company; the Risk Management Committee (R.V. Kanoria as Chairman, S.V. Kanoria, S.K. Birla and Group CFO N.K. Nolkha) met twice during FY26.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Pursue the long-term strategic roadmap 'Vision 2030' for sustainable growth in domestic and international markets and enhanced profitability; future expansion plans towards this roadmap are stated to be under way as planned
- Expand existing manufacturing capacities - completed expansion of Pentaerythritol and Resin capacities during the year, with further Phenolic Resin capacity under construction
- Move up the value chain into value-added specialty chemicals by developing two new product platforms, Triacetin and Penta Derivatives, both in advanced stages of implementation
- Drive innovation …
